Samantha —

Follow-up from our call earlier today. Per discussion, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that aligns evaluation milestones to procurement and activation windows for Dedicated/Private capacity. High-level asks and assumptions are below. Please confirm which items you want prioritized in the MAP and any internal approvals that will impact the timing.

Key assumptions (please correct if anything is off):
- Target production go-live window: mid-November 2026 (8–10 week activation window).
- Initial GPU pool target: 6x A100-class equivalents (mix of 80GB and 40GB based on inference mix) for staging + 20% buffer for acceptance and QA load.
- Deployment mode: Private (VPC) preferred; fallback to Dedicated host if calendar or procurement constraints arise.
- SOC 2 evidence we can provide: partial bundle (attached); full audit will be available by Oct if needed.

Requested next steps:
1) Sign off on MAP v1 (attached) or provide edits by Wed 26 Aug EOD PT.
2) Share procurement lead (procurement@vitahealth.com) and estimated PO timeline so we can lock tranche delivery windows.
3) Confirm on-prem install contact and preferred maintenance window (if Private).

I've cc'd Marissa to track MAP edits and Ben to validate sizing and lead-time hedges.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer

Subject: Sizing and lead-time hedges for VitaHealth MAP

Quick note on sizing and procurement hedging:

Sizing assumptions (conservative):
- Baseline inference footprint: 200 qps at 1.2k tokens/session median load.
- Memory per model instance: 35–42 GB working set.
- Concurrency target: 50 reserved worker slots for staging, 150 for production (post second tranche).

Recommendation:
- Start with an 8x 40GB equivalent pool for staging to reduce migration friction; we can fold the mixed 80/40GB plan into Burst capacity once production stabilizes.
- If procurement timing is tight, reserve a short-term Dedicated buffer (pre-paid credit) for 4 nodes to run acceptance tests if hardware delivery will miss the Board date. This buys time for PO/legal without delaying evaluation.

Lead-time notes:
- Typical procurement -> delivery for Private/VPC appliance: 7–9 weeks depending on region and custom networking.
- We can shorten to 4–5 weeks by prioritizing off-the-shelf chassis and leveraging our Dedicated pool for ephemeral capacity while Private is provisioned.

I'll finalize the cost delta sheet and the 'fast-path' Dedicated fallback estimate by Thu EOD. If you want, I can include a short appendix on quantization/packing strategies that reduce memory footprint and may change the pool sizing by ~15%.

—Ben
